case_title: KILAKKATHA PARAMBATH SASI & ORS. v. STATE OF KERALA
neutral_facts: The accused, who were part of an unlawful assembly, assaulted the victim and his brother at a bus stand due to political animosity. The victim sustained grievous injuries and later died in the hospital. The prosecution presented evidence from multiple witnesses, including the victim's brother, who described the incident and the weapons used. The victim's brother was examined by a doctor who found multiple incised wounds on him. The deceased's body was subjected to a post-mortem, which revealed 58 injuries, most of which were incised and cutting wounds. The accused were charged with offenses under Sections 147, 148, 307, 324, and 302 of the IPC. The trial court acquitted all accused, but the High Court reversed the acquittal of four accused, finding the trial court's decision to be perverse. The High Court endorsed the spontaneity of the FIR and found the prosecution's story to be supported by the evidence of multiple witnesses.
